newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN, forensic team to probe alleged Zaire massacres.
newsitem.headline: UN, forensic team to probe alleged Zaire massacres.

text.p: U.N. human rights investigators and forensic experts will travel to eastern Zaire next month to probe alleged massacres of Rwandan Hutus and civilians by Tutsi-dominated rebels, a U.N. spokeswoman said on Tuesday.

Therese Gastaut told a briefing that the rebels, who have captured half of Zaire since taking up arms last October, had given the green light for the mission to the eastern border town of Goma. The one-month mission will start on May 4.

The inquiry was demanded by the U.N. human rights investigator for Zaire, Roberto Garreton, who accused the rebels of massacring thousands of Rwandan Hutu refugees and civilians after he visited Goma earlier this month and spoke to witnesses.
Zaire's main human rights group, the Association for the Defence of Human Rights in Zaire (Azadho), has also alleged big massacres by the rebels in Hutu refugee camps in the Goma area.
The rebels shelled and overran the camps late last year, after which more than half a million Rwandan Hutus returned home while up to 300,000 others fled deeper into Zaire.
The Hutus fled to Zaire after Tutsi rebels ended the Hutu-led genocide of minority Tutsis in Rwanda in 1994, during which many among the refugees killed or watched others kill.

The U.N. commission of inquiry will include Garreton and two other U.N. investigators and three U.N. human rights officials from Geneva. They will be joined by three forensic scientists who will stay in Goma for a month, Gastaut said.
The supreme U.N. human rights forum which ended its annual meeting in Geneva last week has asked the commission of inquiry to report to the U.N. General Assembly in New York by June 30.
But U.N. officials said member states had yet to come up with the financing needed for the mission.

Garreton's attempts to visit several massacre sites in Goma had been thwarted by the rebels, and it remains to be seen whether they will allow Western forensic experts to dig up mass graves in the area for a whole month.
The investigators have yet to decide which mass graves should be excavated in eastern Zaire, where the rainy season is certain to complicate forensic work.
